meta.description: Download large datasets from NCBI efficiently using EPost, history server, batching, rate limiting, and retry logic. Use when bulk-fetching tens of thousands of sequences, pulling all results of a large ESearch, designing reproducible pipelines, comparing E-utilities to NCBI Datasets v2 CLI, or implementing checksum-validated downloads. Encodes WebEnv TTL (~8h), EPost 200-ID limit, retmax caps, parallelization design, and integrity verification.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 9 inputs used real, live NCBI data (real accessions, real PMIDs, real counts). No fabricated DOI/PMID/statistic anywhere, including the two re-auditor-added inputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure data-retrieval-engineering skill; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-facing content anywhere in scope.

methodological_ground.detail: Retrieval-strategy selection, rate-limit math, and ToS guidance remain methodologically sound; the new >1,000,000/'entire database' escape hatch is methodologically correct and independently confirmed not to over-trigger below its stated threshold (Input 9).

code_usability.detail: Both pre-fix Research Veto failures are fixed and independently re-verified live, not by inspection: (1) examples/robust_download.py's checkpointed_download() now detects a real, freshly-forged expired-WebEnv <ERROR> body, decodes it correctly, refreshes the session, and completes (368/368 records) -- confirmed in this audit's Input 5 using a different forged query_key than the fix log's own verification. (2) examples/batch_fasta.py's integrity-check block now guards the zero-count case; confirmed twice -- once via the shipped script's replaced query (INS[GENE], 4 real records, Input 4-equivalent regression) and once via a genuinely different zero-hit query engineered by this audit (Input 8), proving the guard itself works and is not merely avoided by luck of query choice. SKILL.md's own inline checkpointed_batch_download() was independently extracted (not trusted from the fix log) and confirmed to already carry the same decode guard, then live-tested under a fresh forged-WebEnv condition (Input 2) with full recovery.

functional_suitability.note: Both pre-fix crash cases are fixed and re-verified; the decision matrix now covers the full record-count range from <200 IDs to >1,000,000/'entire database' with no remaining soft-only gap.

reliability.note: All three example scripts and SKILL.md's own inline pattern now recover cleanly from a real forged WebEnv-expiry and from a genuine zero-hit query. One point retained: no committed regression test guards either fix against future urllib/Biopython/NCBI response-shape drift (same gap class noted in this env's entrez-link re-audit).

performance_context.note: Unchanged: SKILL.md grew slightly (new decision-matrix row + field-tag note + moved Setup block) while usage-guide.md shrank by the same amount (redundant sections removed); net footprint roughly flat and still table-driven.

agent_usability.note: The prior Escape Hatches gap (soft 'consider' at extreme scale) is closed with an explicit, quantified hard-stop row matching the existing worker-concurrency cap's phrasing pattern.

human_usability.note: Forgiveness is now strong: both examples that previously failed with raw stack traces on foreseeable real-world cases (0-count query, expired session) now either recover or fail cleanly with a printed message. One point retained for a pre-existing, unrelated clarity nit found in this audit (see P2): the '>100,000 sequences' bracket's own phrasing ('chunk if E-utils still') is grammatically truncated.

security.note: Unchanged: no hardcoded real secrets, no code execution of user input, query strings go into GET params only.

maintainability.note: The redundancy pass (usage-guide.md's 'What the Agent Will Do' and 'Tips' sections removed, Setup moved into SKILL.md) verified line-by-line against SKILL.md: every point is restated, nothing unique was lost. Testability still docked for the same reason as Reliability -- no committed test for either fix.

agent_specific.note: The record-count escape hatch is precise: fires correctly on a genuine 'entire database' request (Input 7) and does not over-trigger on a large-but-sub-threshold 800,000-record request (Input 9). One point retained for the same phrasing nit noted under Human Usability, which sits in the adjacent (still soft, correctly so) >100,000 bracket.

key_strengths: Both flagship P0 crashes (WebEnv-expiry bytes/str decode failure in robust_download.py; zero-hit-query FileNotFoundError in batch_fasta.py) are fixed and independently re-verified live under fresh test conditions the fixer did not use -- a differently-forged bad QueryKey against a different real query, and a genuinely different zero-hit gene query -- not just a re-run of the fixer's own replacement queries.

SKILL.md's inline checkpointed_batch_download() was independently extracted and read from the worktree (not trusted from the fix log's line-number claim), confirmed to already carry the same decode guard, and live-tested under a fresh forged-WebEnv condition with full recovery.

The new P1 escape-hatch row is precise, not a blunt instrument: it fires correctly on a genuine 'entire database, 20 workers' adversarial request and correctly does not over-trigger on a large-but-sub-threshold 800,000-record request, which still needs the softer 'Consider FTP/Datasets CLI' guidance.

Everything the fix pass did not touch -- batch_by_ids.py's EPost/WebEnv chunking and its 200/201-ID boundary guard -- still runs unmodified and correctly (261 real records recovered, 0 loss), confirming the fix was correctly scoped and introduced no regression.

recommendations.title: ">100,000 sequences" decision-matrix row has a grammatically truncated clause
recommendations.problem: The row's Strategy column reads 'Consider FTP mirror or Datasets CLI; chunk if E-utils still' -- the clause after the semicolon is incomplete, unlike every other row in the same table.
recommendations.root_cause: Pre-existing wording gap, unrelated to and unchanged by this fix pass (confirmed identical in the git diff between the pre-fix and fixed commits).
recommendations.fix: Complete the clause, e.g. 'chunk if E-utils is still the chosen path' or 'chunk into batches if still using E-utils at this scale.'

recommendations.title: No committed regression test for either P0 fix
recommendations.problem: The bytes-decode guard and the zero-count guard are both verified only by manual audit runs (this one and the fix log's own); nothing in the repo would catch a regression if a future Biopython/urllib/NCBI response-shape change reintroduced either failure mode.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill (like its siblings in this folder) ships no test suite -- verification is audit-driven, not CI-driven.
recommendations.fix: Add a small pytest module (or a documented manual-check script) that mocks a bytes-typed handle body containing '<ERROR>' and a Count=0 ESearch response, asserting both code paths recover/no-op without raising.
